top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz) has the cleanest credit line among the proposals: two names, each tied to a specific body of work (Melitz 2003 and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple). The framework is over twenty years old, has been tested on firm-level data in many countries, and is standard across trade, macro and industrial organisation. I would word the citation around the selection and reallocation mechanism, with no welfare magnitude and no claim to the exporter-premia facts, because the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum lineage is uncredited. That lineage and the functional-form dependence of the welfare gains are real weaknesses, and I do not rank P001 clearly ahead of the others on science. P004 is second because the formal framework and its later sharper designs are mature and broad, although the identification caveats and the overlap with the 2024 prize weigh against it, and Besley is the most contestable name. P002 is third. Its originator trio is separable and durable and has the largest policy footprint, but the choice among eight credited names and the unresolved theory-versus-estimation strand make any cut contestable. P003 is fourth. Autor, Dorn and Hanson are the most checkable and best-identified unit, but the task-framework credit lies partly outside the ballot and aggregate magnitude and persistence remain debated. All four proposals are worth an award, so P000 is last. I do not use explicit-supporter counts as evidence of merit.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile: no documented co-authorship or institutional tie to Helpman, Melitz, Persson, Tabellini, Besley, Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Autor, Dorn or Hanson. Disclosed: my principal co-author Steven Kaplan and my other co-authors are not credited on any proposal. I hold an adjunct appointment at Chicago Booth and am Vice President of the Academy. I have a long committee overlap with Hassler, Krusell, Ellingsen and Svensson, and SSE colleagues on the committee. My field is corporate finance, which is not represented on the slate. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
